1 شَكِسَ , (T, S, Msb, TA,) aor.
شَكَسَ , inf. n. شَكَسٌ (T, Msb, TA) and شَكَاسَةٌ; (T, S, Msb, TA;) or شَكُسَ, aor.
شَكُسَ , (O, K, TA,) inf. n. شَكَاسَةٌ; (O;) He was, or became, refractory, untractable, perverse, stubborn, or obstinate, in disposition: (S, O, K:) or hard in disposition, or illnatured, in behaviour or dealing: (TA:)or evil in disposition, or illnatured, and very perverse or cross or repugnant and averse; syn. شَرِسَ. (Msb, TA. *)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
